feed.title: David Millard
feed.subtitle: Research portfolio of David Millard, a Ph.D. student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Rochester.

entry.title: Presented Federated IRL Work at L4DC 2026

link.title: Presented Federated IRL Work at L4DC 2026

entry.content: I attended the 8th Annual Learning for Dynamics & Control Conference (L4DC 2026) at the University of Southern California, where I presented our work, Can Optimal Transport Improve Federated Inverse Reinforcement Learning?. The paper introduces an optimal transport-based approach for combining locally learned reward functions across heterogeneous agents.

entry.title: Joined the Human-Centered Computing Lab at the University of Rochester

link.title: Joined the Human-Centered Computing Lab at the University of Rochester

entry.content: I’m excited to share that I joined the Human-Centered Computing Lab at the University of Rochester under the advisement of Distinguished Professor Dr. Mark Bocko. I look forward to contributing to the lab’s research and beginning this new collaboration.

entry.title: Presented PEARL at the 2026 Joint Mathematics Meetings

link.title: Presented PEARL at the 2026 Joint Mathematics Meetings

entry.content: I attended the 2026 Joint Mathematics Meetings in Washington, D.C., where I gave a talk in the SIAM Minisymposium on Recent Advances in Numerical Linear Algebra. I presented our work, PEARL: Preconditioner Enhancement through Actor-critic Reinforcement Learning, which develops a reinforcement learning approach for learning matrix preconditioners.

entry.title: Selected as an AI-PROWIL IRES Scholar

link.title: Selected as an AI-PROWIL IRES Scholar

entry.content: I’m honored to have been selected as an AI-PROWIL IRES Scholar for the Fall of 2025! Through this program, I’ll conduct collaborative research with University West in Trollhättan Sweden, focusing on real-time deviation control for additive manufacturing processes.

entry.title: Accepted to SURF Research Fellowship
entry.content: I’m excited to share that I’ve been accepted into the SURF Research Fellowship! As part of this opportunity, I’ll continue my work on applying conformal prediction in function space, a direction that bridges rigorous uncertainty quantification with the expressive power of scientific machine learning models.
